summary: Takushu Sugimoto specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Tohoku University, studying under teachers including Ensho Kanakura and Birendra Prasad Sinha, and held professorships at Kanazawa, Komazawa, and Kinjo Universities.

Tan Chung (1929–2024) was a scholar of Sinology, history and archaeology, and Indology. He served as Professor of Chinese at the University of Delhi (~1964–1978) and Head of Chinese and Japanese Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1978–1994).

Tansen Sen works in history and archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Peking University under Yinzeng Geng and earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, later holding a post at Baruch College (attested 2003).

Tao Jiang is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University under doctoral supervisor Shigenori Nagatomo, and was an associate professor of religion at Rutgers University (attested 2011).
Tao Jin is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who earned a PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 2008 under doctoral supervisor Alexander L. Mayer.
Tao Pan is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He completed a BA at Fudan University in 2010 and earned a Magister Artium at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich.
Tarab Tulku (1934–2004) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a curator at the Royal Danish Library (~1967–1998) and held a post at the University of Copenhagen (~1968–1998).

Tarif Khalidi is a historian and religious studies scholar. Educated at University College, Oxford (~1957–1960) and the University of Chicago (~1963–1970), he held academic posts at the American University of Beirut (~1970–1996) and the University of Cambridge (~1996–2002).

Tarthang Tulku is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy figure who studied under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Chokyi Lodro. He founded the Nyingma Institute, served as Head Lama there (~1972), and held posts at Padma Ling and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Tashi Tsering is a Tibetologist, historian, and linguist. He founded and directed the Amnye Machen Institute (~1992) and held positions at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 1985–1995) and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014–2019).
Tatiana Oranskaia is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1967–1972) and served as a professor at the University of Hamburg (~2001–2016).

Tatsugen Sato (1924–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He served on the faculty of Komazawa University (~1972–1995) as assistant professor and professor, with additional teaching posts at Ryukoku University (attested 1974) and Tokai University.
Tatsuhiro Saito is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Nikaya Buddhism Thought Study Group.
Tatsuo Nishida (1928–2012) worked in linguistics, Tibetology, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1948–1953), where he later served as a professor (attested 1996).

Tavivat Puntarigvivat specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned an MA from the University of Hawaii, conducted research at Kyoto University, and held posts at Mahidol University (attested 2005) and the World Buddhist University (attested 2013).
Tej Ram Sharma is an Indologist and historian who completed his doctoral thesis at Banaras Hindu University in 1968 and held a post at Himachal Pradesh University (~1976).

Tensei Kitabatake (1928–2024) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He served there as a professor (~1970–1997) and held additional posts at Otani, Gifu Shotoku Gakuen, Kyoto Women's, and Tenri Universities.
Tenshin Tanouye (1938–2003) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under traditional teacher Sogen Omori and founded Chozen-ji.
Tenzin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under MA supervisor Hanna Havnevik and completed a Master of Philosophy at the University of Oslo (attested 2008).

Tenzin Dorjee is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Geshe Lobsang Tsephel, Geshe Sonam Rinchen, and Geshe Dawa. He worked as a translator at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and General Secretary at Pullahari Monastery.
